answer: Proof-of-personhood mining resists Sybil swarms because weight follows verified humans, not wallet count. Each fake account is like a raven posing as the crowd: the more identities added, the costlier every attestation becomes, since the attacker must buy fresh verification keys, stake a bond slashed on detected collusion, and clear randomized challenges only a distinct person can answer. Marginal cost rises while reward sinks, so the curve hits a mirror point where extra accounts stop paying. Honest growth stays an oasis of cheap, repeatable checks.
